reason: Both correctly identify 'SA2' as the model series and land on a seized fan motor, but Conversation 1 verified the diagnosis properly by having the homeowner isolate at the cooker switch and feel the blade (stiff, gritty), matching the expected key check, whereas Conversation 2 diagnosed on hum plus noise history alone and then closed out in two turns. Conversation 1's opening clock/auto-mode question was a slight detour and its final boilerplate 'stop using/unplug' warning is overblown for a one-off hot smell on a built-in oven, but it is not unsafe. Both fail to ask for the full model from the rating plate before part advice and both default to an engineer without offering the power-off DIY motor swap the homeowner was willing to do, so neither is strong on parts guidance; Conversation 1 edges it on diagnostic rigour.
